instructions:
You are performing one bounded phase of the independent chronology workflow.
The host owns publication. Never certify your own repairs. Do not re-extract
names/mentions, rewrite translations, clone the corpus, or call another paid API.

Use the supplied sealed evidence and your assigned output path. Do not create a
repository clone or worktree for this job. When using a shared host checkout, write
only the assigned review/repair artifact; the host owns validation, source changes,
Git operations and publication. Separate reviewer conversations provide independence.

Historical rules: date the named person's OWN event, not a descendant's action,
later quotation, republication, or commemoration. Read the Chinese; the English
and previous model assertions are not independent evidence. Verify conversions
against a primary passage and a reliable calendar reference, including the ruler,
polity, reign and repeated era names. Preserve competing readings. Never infer
twins from 同生 in a maternal list. Preserve age reckoning; do not automatically
convert traditional inclusive age into a precise birth year. Conventional regnal
year labels need not equal the Gregorian year of every month/day within them.
There is no year zero. Use BC/AD. Keep birth/death separate from activity.
Preserve later reception as its own event, not living activity: use event kind
retrospective-reference, or receptionType: retrospective on a narrower honor/work
claim. This does not change the posthumous-name alias kind. Record
the reception's own date, source and subject role. Retrospective does not imply
dead; there is no separate posthumous reception category. A later-written biography
can still attest an earlier life event. Do not use reception dates as life dates
or active hints, and do not discard the later reference when repairing them.
For verified month/day events, normalize Western years/bounds to proleptic
Gregorian and state that convention in the conversion evidence. Check the
converter's calendar setting: Academia Sinica defaults to Julian before 1582,
which can change the Western year near New Year. Retain the Chinese date and
identify Julian witnesses explicitly. Do not apply a fixed offset across
centuries or pretend a reign-year-only label specifies a Gregorian event date.

Use westernBounds with before/onOrBefore/after/onOrAfter positive BC/AD year
objects for genuine one-sided knowledge. An event after an accession in AD 479
can still occur in AD 479: onOrAfter 479, not after 479. Never invent a second
endpoint or turn a bound into an exact year. Preserve relative event sequence.
An unresolved source date requires unresolved:true and a substantive
unresolvedReason, not a guessed year. Research blocks approval; report it honestly.

Distinguish a positively attested, genuinely undated fact from an unresolved
asserted date. In a scoped repair, use an attestation value with
undatedSourceAttestation:true and a source-specific event of at least 20 characters;
it must contain no sourceDate, qualitative, Western-date or unresolved fields.
Preserve the subject, facts and source evidence. Preserve a stated age and its
existing reckoning: an undated age claim may use the same marker and event in its
dateContext. Age five does not supply a calendar year, birth year or reign-wide
activity interval. Check all supplied evidence before changing active hints;
explicitly undated evidence alone does not justify inventing a hint. Reviewers
must still check these items. Do not merely clear unresolved flags: explain the
source-supported replacement. This pathway does not resolve a genuinely disputed
source date, conversion, event owner or conflicting witness; retain the appropriate
supported uncertainty or research hold.

Supported value examples (retain each claim's person and evidence; preserve the
existing sui reckoning in the age example):
Attestation: {"undatedSourceAttestation":true,"event":"Emperor Wu loved Sima Yu and kept him at his side; no calendar date is stated."}
Age: {"age":5,"reckoning":"sui","dateContext":{"undatedSourceAttestation":true,"event":"The crown prince was five when he pulled the emperor by his robe into the darkness; no calendar date is stated."}}

INDEPENDENT-REVIEW:
Read every ownedUnits entry for omitted births, deaths, ages and date context.
Check every ownedItems entry, and check each ownedPeople record for missing or
incoherent chronology in the supplied evidence. Context-only units are read-only;
other jobs own their completeness checks. Identify the owner of every dated
event and justify each endpoint in your reason. A date window must describe
uncertainty about an event, not activity throughout a dynasty. Check active hints
against supported personal events. Later posthumous events must not feed life dates.
Do not approve unsupported chronology merely because it looks plausible.

Return JSON with jobId (input id), sourceHash, extractionHash, reviewedAt (ISO),
reviewer:{name,independentOfExtractor:true}, summary (substantive),
reviewedUnits (exact ownedUnits), itemChecks, personChecks, findings, references.
Every check has id, verdict (supported/incorrect/research-blocked), reason, and
evidence:[{unit,quote}] containing a contiguous exact Chinese substring of the cited
source unit. Never join disjoint passages with ellipses; use separate evidence
entries for disjoint passages. Item checks additionally
have event describing whose event is being dated. This is required for **every**
item check, including `hints-pNNN` active-date-hint rows: give a source-specific
English sentence of at least 10 characters that identifies the named person's own
event (or states that the hint lacks such an event). Do not omit it merely because
the item is a hint rather than a claim. Include exactly ownedItems and
ownedPeople, with no duplicates. Even failed jobs must finish their owned checks
or retain work for continuation; they cannot silently omit a difficult item.
Every failed check has an actionable finding:
{items:[affected item/person IDs],problem,action}. Supported jobs have findings: [].
Keep each check's reason concise and self-contained, with at least 20 characters
after trimming whitespace of substantive, source-specific explanation, not padding:
identify its source anchor and why the date is supported or defective. Do not
lengthen reasons unnecessarily. Put shared research and conversion
explanations once in findings or references instead of repeating paragraphs.
Retain every owned check, its event owner, and exact per-check Chinese evidence.
External research references use {kind:"external",url,title,quote,sourceHash,
accessedAt,reason}; sourceHash is 'sha256:' plus SHA-256 of the short exact excerpt.
Verify the page before citing it; keep quotations short and copyright-compliant.
Do not invent a reference or claim an external source was read when it was not.

REPAIR-PROPOSAL:
Resolve the supplied findings by reading their Chinese evidence and doing any
necessary targeted research. Return {sourceHash,extractionHash,changes:[...]}.
Each change has a substantive source-based reason and one of these forms:
{kind:"replace",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_ROW,after:REVISED_ROW,reason}
{kind:"remove",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_ROW,reason}
{kind:"add",after:[personId,"attestation"|"birth"|"death"|"age",value,certainty,[unitIds]],reason}
{kind:"add-reception-event",after:[personId,"event-participation",value,certainty,[unitIds]],reason}
{kind:"date-context",id:"claim-N",before:EXACT_INPUT_DATE_CONTEXT_OR_NULL,after:REVISED_DATE_CONTEXT,reason}
{kind:"hints",personId,before:EXACT_OLD_HINT_ARRAY,after:NEW_HINT_ARRAY,reason}
Claim rows are compact five-element arrays. Replacements keep subject/predicate.
Use date-context only for an existing non-life claim. Its before value is exactly
claims[id][2].dateContext, or null when absent; its after value is only the revised
date-context object, never a complete claim row. It may change only sourceDate,
westernYear, westernInterval, westernBounds, unresolved, and unresolvedReason.
Copy an existing event description verbatim. The host retains the claim's subject,
predicate, certainty, evidence, and other non-date fields unchanged. Do not remove
or invent an event, or use date-context for attestation, birth, death, or age rows.
Do not modify names, roles, mentions, family links or translation text. Preserve
legitimate posthumous reception as an event, but remove it from personal activity.
Use add-reception-event with an explicit retrospective classification
as described above. Remove or correct the misleading life claim separately.
Do not invent a date for an undated reference or rewrite unrelated event fields.
All necessary operations must be in changes; do not leave required companion
records in hostRequiredChanges or similar side lists. If the supported operations
cannot represent the complete repair, return blocked:true and explain the gap.
Synchronize hints with corrected chronology. Use only existing person IDs and
known source-unit IDs. Avoid unnecessary edits. The next reviewer receives the
resulting claims independently and must establish their support from the source.
If research cannot resolve a finding, return {blocked:true,reason:...}; do not
delete a person or fabricate a date to get a passing result.
For person checks, compare all supplied items and contextItems for that person,
including dates elsewhere in the chapter. Context items are read-only evidence;
do not emit itemChecks for IDs outside ownedItems. Report contradictions or
missing narrative context instead of certifying a person from an isolated event.
Keep supplementary research targeted to an existing date defect, a local omission,
or a needed conversion. Do not expand this audit into new biographies or add every
external life date you encounter. Preserve genuinely conflicting witnesses as
explicitly supported uncertainty when possible; neither choose a winning date nor
create false precision to clear a finding. An unsupported conversion remains a hold.

Retrospective is the sole later-reception category, including commemorations and
references after a known death. Use kind `retrospective-reference` or, on a narrower
honor/work claim, receptionType `retrospective`. Do not require proof of death,
introduce a posthumous subtype, or change the separate `posthumous-name` alias kind.
repairContract: A finding label is a coverage indicator, not necessarily a claim-row ID: target only IDs actually present in claims. For attestation, birth, death, or age rows, chronology changes MUST use kind "replace" with before copied verbatim from claims[id] and a complete after claim row; never use date-context. Claim certainty is exactly one of "explicit", "explicit-event-contextual-date", "strongly-inferred", "uncertain", "derived", or "textual-variant"; never write informal labels such as "inferred" or "contextual". For an explicitly undated source attestation, set undatedSourceAttestation:true directly on that complete after claim value—never use an invented undated field. Its event MUST be one source-specific English string of at least 20 characters (not an object), and it may carry no sourceDate, western date, unresolved field, or other temporal field. For any other row, replace or remove also copy before verbatim from claims[id]. date-context is permitted only for non-life rows: before must be exactly claims[id][2].dateContext (or null) and after must be only the replacement dateContext object. Copy any existing non-temporal dateContext fields, including event, verbatim into after; only sourceDate, westernYear, westernInterval, westernBounds, unresolved, and unresolvedReason may be added, removed, or changed. Put research explanation in reason, never in custom keys such as competingSourceDate, westernCalendar, or conversionEvidence. An add-reception-event MUST be an event-participation row with a nonempty kind such as retrospective-reference. If it supplies receptionType, its value must literally be "retrospective"; "posthumous" is not a valid receptionType. Include any role/action supported by the source. A westernInterval is exactly {start:{era:"AD"|"BC",year:positive integer,precision:"year"|"circa"},end:{era:"AD"|"BC",year:positive integer,precision:"year"|"circa"}}; use no westernYear or westernBounds alongside it. Every western bound is {era:"AD"|"BC",year:positive integer,precision:"year"|"circa"}; never use an ad field. Western years, interval endpoints and bounds use only year or circa precision; preserve finer dates in sourceDate. Non-legendary people with active-date hints require a matching AD/BC hint and a Western attestation unless the sealed source is genuinely undated. Retained chronology can require a qualified hint: westernBounds.onOrAfter AD 355 maps to on or after AD 355, not an empty hint or exact AD 355. Check every retained claim for that person before clearing hints. Put all hint changes last, after claim edits and reception additions. The host preserves every non-date claim field; never send a full claim row for date-context.

findings.problem: Han's retrospective invocation of the late king in AD 344 is recorded as Hui's living activity from 307 to 333.
findings.action: Remove the life attestation, add a retrospective-reference event for p164 dated AD 344 (Han's dying speech), and clear the hint.

findings.problem: There are duplicate person records for the same individuals (Murong Han, Murong Hui, Duan Liao, Murong Huang), which splits their chronologies.
findings.action: The host should merge or link the duplicate identities in the identity workflow. That is outside this date repair.

findings.problem: The Duan Liao-Murong Huang war and remonstrance are dated 338-339. ZZTJ files the remonstrance under 337 (遼數與皝相攻), and it precedes the fall of Lingzhi in 338.
findings.action: Replace the window with westernBounds onOrBefore AD 338 (onOrAfter 333, Huang's accession, if a lower bound is desired). Remove 339.

findings.problem: He Yan's appointment of Yang Yu is dated 304-311, but He Yan was killed in 304.
Yang Yu joining Duan Jilujuan is dated 318-325. ZZTJ 314 records the flight, and Jilujuan died in the first month of 318.
findings.action: Use westernYear 314 (ZZTJ placement), or bounds onOrAfter 314 and onOrBefore 318.

findings.problem: Yang Yu's death and age window starts in 337, before his attested activity in 338-341.
findings.action: Use westernBounds onOrAfter AD 341 and onOrBefore AD 348 (Huang died in the ninth month of Yonghe 4). Keep age 62 sui with no birth year.

findings.problem: The Longcheng planning is dated only to 342. ZZTJ records Yang Yu building Longcheng in the first month of 341.
findings.action: Use westernInterval 341-342 for the planning event.

findings.problem: The point year 338 is used for events in the twelfth month of Xiankang 4, which may fall in January 339 proleptic Gregorian.
findings.action: Verify the month with a calendar conversion (Gregorian setting). Otherwise use a 338-339 window and keep the Chinese date label.

findings.problem: Omitted dated events: s0213 appointments (twelfth month of Xiankang 4), s0214 campaigns against Goguryeo (342) and Yuwen Gui (344), and s0209 Yan commandery warden (ZZTJ: 北平相, a conflicting witness).
findings.action: Add the claims with their own evidence. Keep the s0209 office variant as a conflicting witness.

findings.problem: Han's mother is given Hui's event and window.
findings.action: Replace with undatedSourceAttestation: Murong Han was born to her as Hui's eldest son by a secondary consort, with no date stated. Clear her hints.

findings.problem: Wang Jun's 領州 is dated from 300. ZZTJ places his assumption of Youzhou in 304, after he killed He Yan.
findings.action: Use westernYear 304 for 領州, or bounds onOrAfter 304 and onOrBefore 314 for Yang Yu's transfer.

findings.problem: Undated facts (幼, 初, 少孤) carry invented windows. Claim-1141 and claim-1143 cite Dan's phrase instead of 少孤.
findings.action: Convert these to undatedSourceAttestation or an undated death with the correct evidence. Remove the hints.

findings.problem: Allusions in speeches c.314 are dated as the ancients' own lifespans or activity.
findings.action: Replace them with retrospective-reference events dated to the c.314 speech. Remove the active hints.

units.zh: 皝乃令曰：「覽封記室之諫，孤實懼焉。
units.en: Huang then issued an order, saying: “On reading the remonstrance of Recorder Feng, I am truly afraid.
units.literal: Huang thereupon ordered, saying: “Having read Secretary Feng’s remonstrance, I truly fear it.

units.zh: 三年，遣其世子俊與恪率騎萬七千東襲夫餘，克之，虜其王及部眾五萬餘口以還。
units.en: In the third year he sent his heir Jun and Ke with seventeen thousand cavalry to raid Puyu eastward; they took it, captured its king and more than fifty thousand of the tribe, and returned.
units.literal: In the third year, sent his heir apparent Jun with Ke leading cavalry seventeen thousand east to raid Puyu, took it, captured their king and division host over fifty thousand mouths and returned.

units.zh: 以永和四年死，在位十五年，時年五十二。
units.en: He died in Yonghe 4 (348 CE) after fifteen years on the throne, aged fifty-two.
units.literal: Died in the fourth year of Yonghe, fifteen years on the throne, age fifty-two sui.

units.zh: 俊僭號，追諡文明皇帝。
units.en: After Murong Jun took the throne he posthumously styled his father Emperor Wenming.
units.literal: When Jun illegitimately assumed imperial title, posthumously honored him as Emperor Wenming.

units.zh: 慕容翰，字元邕，廆之庶長子也。
units.en: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Murong Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.
units.literal: Murong Han, courtesy name Yuanyong, was Hui’s eldest son by a concubine.

units.zh: 廆甚奇之，委以折沖之任。
units.en: Murong Hui prized him and gave him the hardest fighting assignments.
units.literal: Hui greatly wondered at him, entrusted him with the charge of breaking the enemy’s momentum.

units.zh: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
units.en: Duan Liao honored him after his defection.
units.literal: When he fled to Duan Liao, deeply was respected and loved by Liao.

units.zh: 後石季龍征遼，皝親將三軍略令支以北，遼議欲追之，翰知皝躬自總戎，戰必克勝，乃謂遼曰：「今石氏向至，方對大故，不宜復以小小為事。
units.en: Later when Shi Hu campaigned against Duan Liao and Murong Huang personally led an army to raid north of Lingzhi, Duan Liao debated pursuit. Knowing Huang commanded in person and must win, Murong Han told Duan Liao, "Now the Shi are about to arrive and you face a great enemy; you should not again take up small matters.
units.literal: Later Shi Jilong campaigned against Liao; Huang personally led the three armies raiding north of Lingzhi; Liao debated wishing to pursue him; Han knew Huang personally commanded the army, battle must seize victory; thereupon said to Liao: “Now the Shi clan is about to arrive, just facing great enemy; ought not again to take small matters as affairs.

units.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
units.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
units.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.

units.zh: 既至，皝甚加恩禮，
units.en: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.
units.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.

units.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。
units.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.

units.zh: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。
units.en: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.
units.literal: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.

units.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。
units.en: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.
units.literal: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.

units.zh: 仰藥而死。
units.en: He drank the poison and died.
units.literal: Raised poison and died.

units.zh: 陽裕，字士倫，右北平無終人也。
units.en: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, came from Wuzhong in right Beiping.
units.literal: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, was a man of Wuzhong in Right Beiping.

units.zh: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」
units.en: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
units.literal: In youth orphaned, brothers all died early, alone and solitary; although the lineage group none could recognize him, only uncle Dan in youth wondered at him, saying: “This child is not only our gate’s outstanding show, but an instrument to aid the age.”

units.zh: 刺史和演辟為主簿。
units.en: Governor He Yan made him chief clerk.
units.literal: The governor He Yan summoned him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。
units.en: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.
units.literal: Wang Jun held the province, transferred to aide in the bureau of administration, envied yet could not employ him.

units.zh: 石勒既克薊城，問棗嵩曰：「幽州人士，誰最可者？」
units.en: After Shi Le took Jicheng he asked Zao Song, "Among the gentlemen of Youzhou, who is most worthy?"
units.literal: After Shi Le took Ji city, asked Zao Song, saying: “Youzhou gentlemen, who is most worthy?”

units.zh: 北平陽裕，幹事之才。」
units.en: Yang Yu of Beiping for administrative talent.”
units.literal: Beiping’s Yang Yu, talent for handling affairs.”

units.zh: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」
units.en: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
units.literal: Le said: “If like your words, why did Duke Wang not employ them?”

units.zh: 嵩曰：「王公由不能任，所以為明公擒也。」
units.en: Song answered, “Because he could not use them, you captured him.”
units.literal: Song said: “Duke Wang because he could not employ them, therefore became the enlightened lord’s captive.”

units.zh: 勒方任之，裕乃微服潛遁。
units.en: Shi Le meant to employ Yang Yu, who fled in disguise.
units.literal: Le was about to employ him; Yu then disguised himself and slipped away.

units.zh: 時鮮卑單于段眷為晉驃騎大將軍、遼西公，雅好人物，虛心延裕。
units.en: At that time the Xianbei shanyu Duan Juan, who held the Jin titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi, had a refined fondness for men of talent and humbly invited Yang Yu.
units.literal: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.

units.zh: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！
units.en: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
units.literal: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!

units.zh: 眷今召我，豈徒然哉！」
units.en: Duan Juan’s summons is no empty gesture!”
units.literal: Juan now summons me—how could it be vain!”

units.zh: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。
units.en: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.
units.literal: Pan said: “Now Huaxia split and crumbling, the nine provinces in tatters, where tracks reach is only to the Yi River.

units.zh: 少遊有雲，郡掾足以廕後，況國相乎！
units.en: Shaoyou said that a post as commandery clerk was enough to shelter one's descendants; how much more the post of chancellor of a state!
units.literal: Shao You said, a commandery aide suffices to shade posterity—how much more a state chancellor!

units.zh: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」
units.en: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
units.literal: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”

units.zh: 裕乃應之。
units.en: Yang Yu accepted Duan Juan’s offer.
units.literal: Yu thereupon answered him.

units.zh: 拜郎中令、中軍將軍，處上卿位。
units.en: He was named palace director and central army general, ranking among the highest ministers.
units.literal: Appointed Palace Director, Central Army General, occupying the upper minister’s seat.

units.zh: 段遼與皝相攻，裕諫曰：「臣聞親仁善鄰，國之寶也。
units.en: When Duan Liao and Murong Huang clashed, Yang Yu urged, “A state’s greatest treasure is to cherish kindness and befriend one’s neighbors.
units.literal: Duan Liao and Huang attacked each other; Yu remonstrated, saying: “I have heard that cherishing benevolence and befriending neighbors is the state’s treasure.

units.zh: 遼不從。
units.en: Duan Liao refused.
units.literal: Liao did not follow.

units.zh: 石季龍克令支，裕以郡降，拜北平太守，徵為尚書左丞。
units.en: When Shi Hu seized Lingzhi, Yang Yu surrendered his commandery, was named grand warden of Beiping, then recalled as left assistant in the secretariat.
units.literal: Shi Jilong took Lingzhi; Yu with the commandery surrendered; appointed Beiping grand warden; summoned as Left Assistant to the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 段遼之請迎于季龍也，裕以左丞領征東麻秋司馬。
units.en: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu to send troops to receive him, Yang Yu, while serving as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.
units.literal: When Duan Liao requested that Jilong receive him, Yu, as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.

units.zh: 秋敗，裕為軍人所執，將詣皝。
units.en: Ma Qiu’s defeat left Yang Yu a prisoner on his way to Murong Huang.
units.literal: When Qiu was defeated, Yu was seized by soldiers, was about to be brought to Huang.

units.zh: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。
units.en: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.
units.literal: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.

units.zh: 東破高句麗，北滅宇文歸，皆豫其謀，皝甚器重之。
units.en: He helped plan the eastern victory over Goguryeo and the northern destruction of Yuwen Gui, and Huang came to rely on him heavily.
units.literal: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.

units.zh: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。
units.en: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.
units.literal: When moved the capital to Helong, Yu by nature had clever thought; the city walls and palace towers Huang regulated were all Yu’s models.

units.zh: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」
units.en: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”
units.literal: In the beginning, Fan Yang’s Lu Chen always praised him, saying: “I have reached Jin’s clear peace, broadly viewed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise, resolute, faithful in duty and fierce in righteousness—like Yang Shilun, in truth also not many.”

units.zh: 及死，皝甚悼之，時年六十二。
units.en: When he died at sixty-two, Murong Huang mourned him deeply.
units.literal: When he died, Huang greatly mourned him; at the time age sixty-two sui.
